audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1 and 2 read Vladimir while their own whys said 'even' and 'skill'; rows 0, 3 and 4 disagreed with the packet chart.
audit.why: The mirror audit (nautilus__vladimir) set levels 2, 3 and 6 to Nautilus and kept the item rows for Vladimir; the packet chart also gives Nautilus Levels 4-5 and Vladimir Level 1. Nautilus owns the stretch where Titan's Wrath, Riptide and the Staggering Blow root are online together, and level 6 belongs to Depth Charge.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Vladimir / Nautilus / Nautilus / Nautilus / Nautilus / Vladimir / Vladimir across phases[N].side and win[N] as one paired atomic group.

audit.why: Nautilus spikes at level 4 (full kit) and 6 (Depth Charge); Vladimir's are Riftmaker and two items. The item rows were already right.
audit.corrected: Level 6 reasoning rewritten to name Depth Charge instead of claiming Nautilus has no burst answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text claimed you can poke him down at 6 'without fearing a burst answer', and dontsFull[1].d carried a generic template body under the title 'Eat his passive root chain'.
audit.why: Depth Charge is an 825-range shockwave that chases the target, knocks up everyone it passes and stuns on arrival — it does not need him to walk at you. Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against each target, so every re-approach re-arms a root. Riptide is a 7s slow at rank 1 and Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1, which is the real punish window. Vladimir has no dash: Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetable on a 28s rank-1 cooldown is the entire answer, so it must be spent on the engage, not on chip.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, phases[4].why, phases[2].why, phases[1].why, whys[1], whys[2], whys[4] and dontsFull[1].d rewritten with the real abilities and cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'terrain-cuts-retreat' headline reads as though Nautilus builds a wall behind you.
audit.why: Riot's text says Dredge Line colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it — it is a gap-closer over walls, not a wall he places. Written that way it would be a fabricated mechanic.
audit.corrected: Not written. The genuine version — he can Q terrain to close from an angle you did not expect — is covered by holding Pool for the engage.

edits.before: Pool answers his single biggest button — save it for exactly that. Only take the trade when Nautilus's Dredge Line is down.
edits.after: Pool answers his single biggest button — save it for exactly that. Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1; step up only inside it.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Nautilus must walk into your range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Riptide is a 7s slow and his passive roots on his first auto — never trade at melee range.

edits.before: Hemoplague + empowered Q turns mid-game fights into resets. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nautilus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Hemoplague resets fights, but Depth Charge is an 825-range knock-up into a passive root — do not stand alone at 6.

edits.before: Level 2 is even as he gains tools but still can't kill you outright.
edits.after: Level 2 is his — Titan's Wrath shield plus a passive root wins the trade.

edits.before: Level 3 stays skill — the fight hinges on dodging his hook, not raw power.
edits.after: Level 3 is his — Riptide slows on a 7s cooldown and Dredge Line follows it.

edits.before: At 6 Hemoplague and your poke overpower his low kill threat, favouring you.
edits.after: At 6 Depth Charge is an 825-range knock-up into his full combo, favouring him.

edits.before: Hemoplague flips it back to you: Nautilus is low-damage and immobile, so once you have R you can E-Q poke him down and all-in when his Q is on cooldown without fearing a burst answer.
edits.after: Level 6 is his: Depth Charge is an 825-range chase that knocks you up, stuns, and chains into a Staggering Blow root. Hold Sanguine Pool for the moment it lands, not for his poke.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first auto — break contact to reset it.

notes: tldr, winCon, report[0].t and report[1].t all promise 'Q %HP-poke'. Transfusion is flat magic damage in Riot's text with no percent-health component anywhere in Vladimir's kit, so this is a fabrication repeated in four fields. I did not rewrite them here because they are champion-level boilerplate that appears on other Vladimir matchups too — it needs one consistent fix across the champion rather than a per-matchup patch.
